The register says applicant: "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH", the document says "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH".

Interesting: Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik (HBM) was acquired by Spectris and renamed to "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" (HBK) around 2021-2022. So these are actually the same legal entity — the company renamed. But per the rules given: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH" vs "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" a rename (same entity) or different entity? In the real world, it's the same legal entity renamed. However, the rules only permit "same-entity" for spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences. A corporate rename to a genuinely different name is not covered by those. The rules say "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity". The task says "decide the relationship and pick the best value for a fused record" — the certificate document is the legal instrument, so best_value should be the document's value for different-entity.

Given the certificate year is 2026, the issuer would print the current legal name "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH" while the register has the older name. The certificate is the legal instrument, so best_value = "Hottinger Brüel & Kjaer GmbH".

Verdict: different-entity. Why: the names differ beyond spelling/accent drift — the register carries the pre-rename name while the certificate bears the current legal name, so per rules treat as different-entity and adopt the document value.

Hmm, but one could argue same-entity due to corporate rename. The rule's "same-entity" category is narrowly defined as spelling drift etc. The rename is a genuinely different name string. The instruction: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's)". So verdict different-entity, best_value from document.
